>## What this PR does / why we need it:

## AWS e2e failure root cause

The initial fix used `e2eutil.IsGreaterThanOrEqualTo(Version50)` to predict `rhel-10` for OCP 5.0 payloads. This worked on GKE but failed on AWS because the OCP 5.0 nightly payload on AWS still ships RHEL 9 RHCOS — the RHCOS RHEL generation transition doesn't happen uniformly across platforms.

The CI release image for this PR is built from `main` which targets OCP 5.0, so `releaseVersion` is `5.0.0`, but the actual RHCOS on AWS nodes reports `Red Hat Enterprise Linux CoreOS 419.x` (RHEL 9). The version-based prediction is fundamentally unreliable during RHCOS transitions.

## Changes made

**Made the test payload-agnostic** — assert the stream is set and recognized rather than predicting the exact value:

1. **`NodePoolOSImageStreamDefaultStatusTest`**: Replaced version-derived expected stream with `osImageStreamSetPredicate()` that accepts any recognized stream (`rhel-9` or `rhel-10`). The test still validates the controller populated the field from Machine NodeInfo.OSImage — it just doesn't predict which RHEL generation the payload ships.

2. **`NodePoolOSImageStreamExplicitDefaultNoRolloutTest`**: Instead of predicting the default stream, polls for `status.osImageStream` to be set (via `EventuallyObject` + `osImageStreamSetPredicate()`), then reads the actual value from status to use for the no-rollout patch. This is both payload-agnostic and resilient to controller timing.

Hey @bryan-cox — we have [#9099](https://github.com/openshift/hypershift/pull/9099) which overlaps significantly with this PR. It's part of the broader dual-stream RHEL 9/10 feature ([CNTRLPLANE-3871](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/CNTRLPLANE-3871)) and addresses the same test issues plus more:

1. **Same fix**: removes the hardcoded `rhel-9` expectation and makes it version-aware
2. **CEL immutability bug**: `NodePoolOSImageStreamExplicitDefaultNoRolloutTest` cleanup tries to remove `osImageStream` which CEL blocks ("cannot be removed once set"). We rewrote it to create its own NodePool instead of mutating the default one
3. **Upgrade verification**: moved `verifyOSImageStreamAfterUpgrade` from the upgrade tests into `nodepool_osimagestream_test.go` as a dedicated test
4. **Dedicated CI job**: all osImageStream tests now run under a dedicated `e2e-v2-aws-techpreview-osimagestream` job ([openshift/release#82438](https://github.com/openshift/release/pull/82438)) where the hosted cluster has TechPreview, so the MCO actually processes the OSImageStream manifest
5. **Controller changes**: removes StreamRHEL9 hardcode, resolves RHEL stream dynamically via `GetRHELStreamForBootImage`

This is a key piece of the dual-stream RHEL feature — the dependency chain is: release#82438 → hypershift#9099 → api#2950 (FG graduation).

Would you be OK holding this until #9099 goes in? We can pick up the Makefile `test-changed` fix from your PR separately if needed.
